watch.label: The Flying Deuces (1939), full-length copy, about 68 min, directed by A. Edward Sutherland

editorial:
The Flying Deuces is a 1939 Laurel and Hardy feature directed by A. Edward Sutherland. It was produced by Boris Morros Productions and released by RKO Radio Pictures on 3 November 1939. In it Ollie falls for an innkeeper's daughter in Paris and joins the Foreign Legion with Stan to forget her. A creator would want it as a mainstream Laurel and Hardy feature that circulates widely online.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not established here. An Internet Archive uploader says the film is public domain through non-renewal, but that is not a primary record. I did not confirm an absence of renewal in the 1966 or 1967 Catalog of Copyright Entries. Score, story and any restoration additions were not researched. Check the renewal volumes by hand before relying on any copy.
faq: Is The Flying Deuces confirmed public domain in the US?

Not by this dossier. An Internet Archive uploader claims non-renewal, but I did not confirm it in the 1966 or 1967 Catalog of Copyright Entries or the Stanford renewal database. Search those yourself first.
Can I use any copy I find online?

Not safely. Some uploads are colorized, remastered or cut down (one Internet Archive copy runs about 44 minutes against about 68 for another). Any added music, colorization or new titles can carry their own protection even if the underlying film is free.
